title: SGNE-CC v2: Editing 205 Weight Columns in DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B Improves Greedy Accuracy and Reduces Unfinished Responses
domain: math reasoning, code generation, science QA and logic (reasoning-trace termination)

headline_result.text: A hand-derived norm-preserving rotation of 205 mlp.down_proj columns (0.0177% of weights) raised pooled greedy accuracy from 638 to 733 of 1,054 problems (+9.0 pp) but gave no significant gain under T = 0.6 sampling (72.3% to 73.3%, p = 0.4472).
headline_result.quote: With greedy decoding (`T = 0`), correct answers rose from `638` to `733` out of `1,054` (`+9.0 pp`, $p = 6.07 \times 10^{-10}$), responses without a closing reasoning marker fell from `305` to `41`

key_claims.claim: The edit rotates 205 mlp.down_proj columns toward the </think> unembedding direction while preserving column norms; attention, gate/up projections, vocabulary and code are unchanged.
key_claims.quote: Each column is rotated toward the unit reasoning-end direction

key_claims.claim: On full MATH-500 at T = 0, unclosed responses fell from 139 to 16 and the edit gained 74 and lost 19 correct answers.
key_claims.quote: With greedy decoding, responses missing `</think>` fell from `139` to `16`, and responses missing `EOS` also fell from `139` to `16`

key_claims.claim: The greedy MATH-500 gain persists after excluding the 26 calibration problems and the 53 head-inspection problems (421 items: 276 to 321).
key_claims.quote: On the remaining **`421` problems**, the greedy gain persists (`276 → 321`, `+60 / −15`, $p = 1.59 \times 10^{-7}$)

key_claims.claim: Under sampling at T = 0.6 the edit mainly shortens outputs and stabilizes closure rather than raising accuracy.
key_claims.quote: under sampling, the edit acts primarily as length compression (`−33.6%`) and closure stabilization (`29 → 4`; `EOS` cap hits `30 → 4`).

key_claims.claim: The v1 edit on Qwen3.5-0.8B (the MIT test model) is reported as giving 4.0x shorter outputs than MIT-p50c at T = 0.6 with presence penalty 1.5.

limitations_stated.text: At T = 0 the 166 gains come with 71 losses that a single </think> position does not explain.
limitations_stated.quote: `166` newly solved problems are accompanied by `71` losses.

limitations_stated.text: The edited model sometimes emits a second </think> token.
limitations_stated.quote: `SGNE-CC v2` occasionally emits a second `</think>` token (`84` cases at `T = 0`, `83` at `T = 0.6` vs. `0` and `3` in the base model).

limitations_stated.text: The v1/v2 comparison mixes different presence penalties and grading parsers, and architecture and model-size effects are not isolated.
limitations_stated.quote: note that the two studies use different presence penalties and math-grading parsers, and architecture vs. model-size effects are not isolated

notes_for_review: A hand-designed (mechanistic, non-LLM-editor) weight edit that targets the same failure as MIT's Qwen3.5-0.8B MATH-500 edit: reasoning traces that never close </think>. The release documents that the large greedy gain mostly disappears under the recommended T = 0.6 sampling (+1.0 pp, p = 0.4472), which supports reading such edits as termination fixes rather than reasoning gains. Evidence is a single seed per setting with exact McNemar tests, calibration/inspection items excluded in sensitivity checks, and checksummed per-item traces; there is no random-direction control and no fine-tuning baseline. No LLM is described as writing the edit, so it serves as a non-LLM comparator rather than WSP proper.
